chunks: He said: 'I was given it through knowledge that is with me.' Did he not know that Allah had destroyed from before him among the generations those who were stronger in might than he and more abundant in wealth? And the sinners will not be asked about their sins.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean when it says Pharaoh claimed divinity through his own knowledge?
ai.summary: This narration elucidates Pharaoh's arrogant claim in Surah Az-Zukhruf that his dominion was granted solely due to his personal knowledge and power, contrasting his self-perception with divine reality. It underscores the Shia scholarly understanding that despite his immense strength and wealth, he was destroyed like previous generations, highlighting the transient nature of worldly power. The verse further emphasizes that the sinners will not be questioned about their sins on the Day of Judgment, as their deeds are already well-known to Allah.
